_comment: fux.toml -- POLICY, not corpus. The one schema here that is CONSUMER-FACING:
a human writes this file by hand, so its failure mode is not drift between
two modules but a typo that costs someone an afternoon.
WHAT IS DECLARED HERE AND WHAT IS NOT, because the boundary is the point:
fux.toml       policy -- where things live, how to reach them
.fux/sources/  the CORPUS -- one entry per line, so 5k entries diff and
merge line by line instead of as one TOML array
.fux/tune.toml every knob that changes ORDERING and none that changes the
index, decided by one mechanical test
[sources.url.config] IS DELIBERATELY OPAQUE AND IS NOT DECLARED FIELD BY
FIELD. Fux validates that it is a table and never reads a key inside it --
PEP 518's [tool.*] discipline. Typing `cdp_port` or `settle_ms` into this
schema would breach the adapter cap through the back door: it would put one
fetcher's vocabulary into fux's config surface, where every future fetcher
would have to be argued against it. That is why its type is `dict` and

sources._doc: The `[sources]` table. Everything has a default; the keys exist to be seen rather than to be required.

types_file.doc: OPTIONAL. Absent means the built-in prose allowlist; present REPLACES it entirely -- an absent file never means index-everything and never means index-nothing

_doc: The `[sources.url]` table. Its PRESENCE enables URL ingestion; absent
means fux never imports a fetcher at all.
Three layers resolve every attribute, in one order: the built-in default,
then this table, then the line in `.fux/sources/urls`. A line beats both,
and only ever for its own URL.

fetcher.doc: the file a line with no `fetch=` uses, AND the directory `fetch=cdp` resolves in -- one key carries both, so relocating your fetchers is a one-line change

meta.doc: L5's privacy FLOOR for this source. A line may loosen it to `plain` for one public document; there is deliberately no way to make one line stricter

max_parallel.doc: URLs in flight at once. ⚠ REQUIRED whenever [sources.url] exists (W-85) -- every other key here has a default and this one does not, because a repo that CAN fetch must say how hard in a number a person can read. Below 1 refuses; above the fetcher's declared MAX_PARALLEL is clamped down loudly, because a declaration answers what is SAFE and this answers what is POLITE

config.doc: passed VERBATIM to the fetcher's configure(). Fux never reads a key inside it -- see the note at the head of this file

_doc: The `[agents]` table -- which vendors `fux setup` writes instruction
files for.
DECLARED, NEVER DETECTED. Fux does not sniff the filesystem for a
`.claude/` directory and infer intent from it; a declaration is exact for
the repo it was written in, and a silent convention everywhere else.
`install = []` installs none.

install.doc: any of: claude, codex, copilot, kiro. Absent means all of them; [] means none

_doc: The `[decode]` table -- limits applied while a document is turned into
Markdown.
WHY THIS IS HERE AND NOT IN .fux/tune.toml. tune.toml holds every knob
that changes how results are ORDERED and none that changes what is
INDEXED (ADR-TUNE decision 7). A row limit decides which rows EXIST as
far as the index is concerned, so it is committed config, and
`same sources + same committed config -> same index` is the L3 that
holds.
IT COUNTS DATA ROWS. A header is always kept and never counted -- 20 000
means twenty thousand records, not 19 999 plus a header.
RAISED 500 -> 20 000 ON 2026-09-06. The old hard-coded 500 was a silent
data loss: a 754-row CSV decoded to 500 rows, so a fact in row 600 was
not decoded, not indexed and not citable, with a `*(table truncated)*`
line as the only signal.

max_table_rows.doc: data rows admitted from one table (per SHEET for .xlsx). Default 20000; must be >= 1. Higher costs query latency: refer chunks one passage per row, and rescore is O(passages)

_doc: Keys that once existed and now STOP THE RUN with instructions rather than
being ignored. A silently-ignored key is a config a person believes is in
force and is not.
Both were breaking changes taken deliberately while they were cheapest.
_retired_keys.middleware: renamed to `fetcher`; the file also moved from .fux/middleware/ to .fux/fetchers/
_retired_keys.sources.dirs: the corpus left fux.toml for `.fux/sources/dirs`, one entry per line
_retired_keys.ranking: moved to `.fux/tune.toml` -- it changes ordering, not the index
